s1.headline: Living should not have a price tag.Uncost the cost of living.
s1.subhead:
Uncost is a nonprofit movement to significantly reduce the cost of living by putting AI and robotics to work for humanity.

Technology should make living cheaper, not billionaires richer.

stat1.caption: The median American renter spent 31% of their income on rent and utilities in 2024 — up from 27% in 2001.

stat2.caption: From 2001 to 2024, median rent rose 30% after inflation. The median renter’s income rose just 9%.

stat3.caption: Family health coverage through an employer cost $26,993 in 2025 — workers paid $6,850 of it.

s3.body: Automation, robotics and open-source tools get cheaper and better every year. We work out where they could genuinely lower the cost of essentials — housing, food, energy and more — publish exactly what it would cost and whether it actually worked, and share the results free, so communities can act on them. No jargon, no hype.
s3.headline: Point the tools at the things that keep people alive.

a.body: Models, briefs and playbooks any community can copy, adapt and run. We build the plans and the software; communities build the thing itself.
a.title: Open projects

b.body: A clear, sourced picture of what living actually costs, region by region, and how it’s changing over time.

s4.headline: Open projects, and a dashboard for the true cost of living.

s5.body: Fifteen sectors cover everything a person needs. Year one concentrates on the three where the pressure is heaviest — Shelter, Food and Energy — with Water next.
s5.food: Nutrition, farming, storage, cooking and distribution.
s5.headline: We start where the money actually goes.
s5.note: Water is next. The other eleven are mapped and waiting — status is sequencing, not importance.
s5.shelter: Housing, land use, construction, heating and cooling.

s6.body: Every figure here carries its source, its date and its region. Negative results are published as prominently as wins. Everything we produce is open for anyone to use, free — and a person, not an algorithm, is accountable for every claim.
s6.eyebrow: Why you can trust the numbers
s6.headline: If we can’t show where a number came from, we don’t print it.
